1.why: MFA routes resolve the account only via getSession(authenticated) and accountForSession(session.accountId); no client-supplied account id is trusted.

2.why: Identity OTP is bound to the pending session hash, TOTP to the account secret, and backup codes to per-account hashes, so a code does not work for another user.

3.why: Enabling MFA only updates account.mfa status/secrets and never deletes or rotates other existing sessions in the sessions Map.

4.why: TOTP secret is stored with AES-GCM encryptSecret; backup codes are stored only as hashValue() digests with used flags.

5.why: Tokens, OTP digits, Base32 secrets, and recovery codes all use crypto.getRandomValues via randomToken/secureInt.

6.why: Session id is only in the __Host-mfa_session HttpOnly cookie; csrf and secrets stay in JS memory/DOM responses, not localStorage or non-HttpOnly cookies.

7.why: Server validates email, phone, 6-digit OTP, and recovery-code shape before use; body size/type are bounded in requestBody.

8.why: UI sets dynamic values with textContent and APIs return JSON; no innerHTML of user input, limiting XSS execution.

9.why: Handler never issues redirects; only allow-listed paths are served and requests with query strings are rejected.

10.why: headersFor sets CSP (frame-ancestors 'none'), HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, and X-Frame-Options DENY on responses.

11.why: cookieHeader always sets HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict on the session cookie.

12.why: genericError and the top-level catch return a fixed message with no stack traces; secrets are not written to logs or URLs (query strings rejected).

13.why: Identity codes are single-use with identityExpiresAt; TOTP rejects reused counters; backup codes flip used after success.

14.why: Identity, TOTP, and recovery paths increment failure counters and set lockUntil after VERIFICATION_FAILURE_THRESHOLD attempts.

15.why: rotateAuthenticatedSession issues a new session id on verify; idle/absolute timeouts are enforced in getSession; logout deletes the session and clears the cookie.
